Backends: the table types the verbs accept

Source: R/backend.R
backend.Rd

The conversion verbs run on a data.frame, a tibble, a data.table, a dtplyr lazy table or an arrow Dataset/Table/query, and return results in the caller's type; lazy inputs stay lazy unless collected. These functions are that contract, exposed so a dimension package built on nestedscales can accept the same inputs as the core verbs.

backend_of(data, arg = "data")

backend_is_lazy(backend)

backend_schema(data, backend = NULL)

backend_lazy(data, backend = NULL)

backend_scan(data, backend = NULL, columns = NULL, filter = NULL)

backend_distinct(data, columns, backend = NULL)

backend_pull(table)

backend_restore(table, backend, collect = NULL)

backend_bind_rows(
  parts,
  use_dt = requireNamespace("data.table", quietly = TRUE)
)

Arguments

data

A data object on any supported backend.

arg

Argument name used in the error message.

backend

A backend name from backend_of(); NULL resolves it from data.

columns

Column names to read; NULL reads every column.

filter

An unevaluated dplyr filter expression (built with rlang::expr()), or NULL for every row.

table

A query or table.

collect

Force materialisation of a lazy result.

parts

List of data frames.

use_dt

Use data.table::rbindlist(). Defaults to whether data.table is installed; an explicit value makes both branches testable.

Value

backend_of() a single string naming the backend; backend_is_lazy() a logical; backend_schema() a zero-row data.frame; backend_lazy() data, wrapped where the backend needs it; backend_scan(), backend_distinct() and backend_pull() a data.frame; backend_restore() the result in the input's class; backend_bind_rows() one data frame, or NULL when every part is empty.

Details

  • backend_of() names the backend of data, and errors on an unsupported input – the one place that message is written.

  • backend_is_lazy() says whether a backend produces queries.

  • backend_schema() describes the columns without scanning the data.

  • backend_lazy() lifts data into a dplyr-compatible carrier for a pipeline (a data.table becomes a dtplyr step when dtplyr is installed).

  • backend_scan() reads the needed columns and rows into memory.

  • backend_distinct() is the distinct rows of some columns, in first-appearance order, read into memory.

  • backend_pull() materialises a query or table as a data.frame.

  • backend_restore() returns a pipeline result in the caller's type.

  • backend_bind_rows() binds chunk results into one frame.

Examples

d <- data.frame(unit = c("U1", "U2", "U2"), v = 1:3)
backend_of(d)
#> [1] "data.frame"
backend_is_lazy(backend_of(d))
#> [1] FALSE
backend_schema(d)
#> [1] unit v   
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
backend_distinct(d, "unit")
#>   unit
#> 1   U1
#> 2   U2
backend_scan(d, columns = "v", filter = rlang::expr(v > 1))
#>   v
#> 1 2
#> 2 3
